one_month_reasoning: No CoreWeave earnings in the window (no Q3 date announced as of Oct 2; Q3 expected in November, outside Oct 31). In-window events: FOMC Oct 27-28 (Polymarket 75% hold / 25% +25bp, $22.3M volume, re-checked Oct 2) against a 5.29% 10y, a headwind for a name adding ~$20B of debt per half-year; hyperscaler Q3 results and 2027 capex commentary in the last week of October (Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon; dates are estimates), which typically move neoclouds 5-15% either way; continued ATM supply (up to 35M shares) and convert-hedge activity around the $97.85 conversion price as mild drags/pins. None gives a directional edge, so I stay near neutral: lognormal centred at $87.6 (slightly below spot for ATM supply) with a monthly sigma of 0.27 (93%/3.5). Round 3: unchanged. The GPU-life research changes long-run cash flows, not anything scheduled before Oct 31, and current rental indices are firm (Silicon Data H100 $2.77 on 1 Oct, +4.9% w/w; Ornn $2.92), so nothing in the window moves on it. Round 4: unchanged. Still no Q3 date announced (Q3-25 results came on Nov 10 with the date announced Oct 27, so Q3-26 most likely falls outside the window). The site and discount-rate work changes long-dated cash flows only; no site delivery (APLD B2's last 75 MW went live Oct 2, already known) or financing event is scheduled inside October.

fair_value.method: 50% DCF ($9: site-built GPU-cohort DCF at 2027-10-01 with signed RPO discounted by counterparty credit (IG 8.1% anchored on DDTL 4.0, OpenAI/Anthropic 10.1%, other ~11%) and everything else at 11.5%; pipeline probability-weighted; floored grid $8.9 split vs $8.1 single; base cell -$27 split / -$29.5 single) + 50% EV/EBITDA ($97: 6.0x x $20.3B NTM adj. EBITDA = $121.9B less $61.5B net debt / 625M) = ~$53. The split rate adds only ~$2/share because by Oct-27 most signed contract cash is 1-4 years out; the bigger change is that the uncontracted pipeline is no longer treated as certain.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-built GPU-cohort DCF at 2027-10-01, split-rate. Contracted fleet = the 2023-27 cohorts (capex $3/10/25.5/37/34B at k 2.7, ~3.94 GW at $10.3M contract revenue per MW), mapped to 40 inventory sites by MW and energisation date; site-specific lease costs (Core Scientific $1.44M, Galaxy $1.9M, Applied Digital $1.8M, Blockfusion $2.2M per MW-yr vs $1.8M generic) and owned shells (Kenilworth, Hammond: no rent, +$6M/MW shell capex). Uncontracted pipeline probability-weighted at WACC: Kenilworth phase 2 200 MW p0.7, Hammond 180 MW p0.6, powered land/options/LOIs 1.5 GW p0.5, NVIDIA-framework increment to 8 GW 2.3 GW p0.2 (expected 1.46 GW vs ~2.65 GW treated as certain in round 3). Signed RPO ($103.7B at 6/30/26; $77B left after 10/1/27) discounted by counterparty tier: IG (Meta/NVIDIA/Microsoft) 8.1%, Jane Street 9.1%, OpenAI/Anthropic 10.1%, other 11.0%, Q3-26 commitments 11.2%; everything else (post-contract, future contracts, refresh, pipeline, terminal) at 11.5%. Base (6-yr life, k 2.7->2.5): revenue 2027-33 $25.2/36.2/41.9/45.1/46.6/46.1/46.9B, adj. EBITDA $15.3/22.0/25.5/27.4/28.0/27.5/28.7B, capex $34/11.6/17.9/19.0/23.6/29.1/30.9B; EV $43.1B single-rate (+$1.35B split) vs $61.5B net debt: -$29.5 single / -$27.3 split per share. Floored grid (life 5-8 x k 2.3-2.7): $8.1 single / $8.9 split -> $9.

inputs_detail.value: 2027-10-01; cohort engine 2023-2060 rebuilt this round from the round-3 specification (reproduces round-3 revenue/EBITDA/FCF to within $0.1B and the grid to within $3-7/share; base -$53 vs -$56 reported), now run per site; new and refresh cohorts earn nothing in their capex year; Gordon terminal on the average of the last L years
inputs_detail.derivation: The brief asks for contracted revenue at contract price for contract term, then a decaying market price, a cash tail and life-consistent refresh capex; a cohort model is the direct way to do that. Q4'27 stub = 25% of 2027 FCF.

inputs_detail.value: 2023 $3B, 2024 $10B, 2025 $25.5B, 2026 $37B, 2027 $34B (the contracted fleet, k 2.7); round-3 growth capex 2028-32 replaced by probability-weighted pipeline cohorts (see Pipeline probabilities); 3% capacity growth from 2033 on the expected base
inputs_detail.derivation: Unchanged from round 2 (2026 guide $35-39B mid; pre-2026 vintages back-solved from gross PP&E; capacity path from 4.2 GW contracted / >$30B exit-2027 run-rate). These targets now set capacity at contract price; actual revenue is lower once cohorts come off contract.

inputs_detail.input: Capex intensity k (capex per $ of annual contract-price revenue)
inputs_detail.value: 2.7x through 2028, 2.5x after; grid 2.3/2.5/2.7
inputs_detail.derivation: Unchanged from round 2 and inside the supervisor's 2.3-2.7x band. Revenue ramp: 10% of a cohort's run-rate in its capex year, 75% the next year, then 100%. Gives 2027 revenue $25.6B vs $26.26B consensus [12]. Cross-check with sites: k 2.7 x $10.3M contract revenue per MW (exit-2026 run-rate $18.5-19.5B / >1.85 GW) = ~$28M per MW, against the supervisor's ~$26.5M gross equipment per active MW.

inputs_detail.value: 90% of each cohort contracted at the contract price: 45% for 4 years, 27% for 5, 18% for 6; 10% sold at market from day one
inputs_detail.derivation: 10-Q: RPO $103.7B, 41% recognised in months 1-24, 39% in 25-48, 20% in 49-78, so contracts run 4 to 6.5 years from start; nearly all revenue is under committed contracts.

inputs_detail.input: Post-contract price path, base (6-yr economic life)
inputs_detail.value: price relative to the cohort's contract price by year of service: 1.00, 0.90, 0.82, 0.78, 0.75, 0.58; retire after year 6 (year-7 price ~0.42 is about cash break-even)
inputs_detail.derivation: Market prices fall ~50% vs launch in the ~18-24 months after the successor ships, then ~10%/yr (H100 composite $6.62 -> $3.34 in 18 months, then flat ~$2.80 [24]; A100 23-39% of launch at year 6 [25,26]; V100 ~5% at year 9). CoreWeave's multi-year contract prices sit ~40-45% below launch-era spot, which is why a 2022-23 H100 cluster re-booked within 5% of its original price [23] and an A100 contract runs into 2029 [22]. Taken alone, that observed path is ~0.9 of contract in year 5 and ~0.6 in year 7, with break-even around year 8-9. I haircut it toward a glut regime (each new generation cuts cost per token 3-10x; Amazon cut some server lives 6->5 yrs [28]) because the 2025-26 evidence comes from a supply- and power-constrained market [21]. Fact-check: Intrator's words are that prior-gen pricing is 'at or above where it was years ago' [47]; the SemiAnalysis composite ran $2.80-2.90 Aug-25 to Apr-26 [24,47]; nothing in the fact-check changes the path.

inputs_detail.value: 5-yr (glut: rents reach cash cost ~year 6): 1.00, 0.80, 0.65, 0.55, 0.45, retire after 5, except the 18% slice on 6-yr contracts, which now runs at contract price to the end of its term and is refreshed then (supervisor correction). 7-yr (scarcity persists, close to observed): 1.00, 0.97, 0.94, 0.92, 0.90, 0.75, 0.60, retire after 7. Also shown: an 8-yr path 1,1,1,1,0.92,0.80,0.66,0.50
inputs_detail.derivation: The 5-yr path follows the research's glut case (Hopper-class rents near cash cost within ~3-4 yrs of launch) and Kerrisdale's 4-5-yr case [27]. The 7/8-yr paths follow the observed 2025-26 rental and recontract data. Kerrisdale's figures could not be verified (fact-check, 403) and are kept only as a description of the bear case.

inputs_detail.input: Cash cost per cohort (cash tail test)
inputs_detail.value: Fixed site cost (power, colocation/lease, site ops) = 30% of contract revenue for pre-2027 cohorts, 28% for 2027+; corporate overhead 10% of actual revenue; adj. EBITDA margin at contract price 60% / 62%
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2-26 adj. EBITDA 59%, with 5-10pp higher contribution on new contracts (Q2 call). A cohort keeps running while price x 0.9 > fixed cost, i.e. above ~0.33 of contract price. That matches the research's cash-margin arithmetic (H100 power+colo ~$0.38/hr vs ~$2.7 rent; V100 at ~break-even). Company margin comes out at 59-60% for 2027-30, dips to ~57-58% in 2031-32 as the 2025-26 cohorts reprice, and averages ~59% in steady state.

inputs_detail.value: When a cohort retires, its contract-price capacity is rebuilt at 0.85 x 2.5 = 2.125x that capacity, in the retirement year; base retirements 2029 $2.4B, 2030 $7.9B, 2031 $20.1B, 2032 $29.1B, 2033 $26.8B
inputs_detail.derivation: 85% of original cost because shells, power and networking are partly reused (round 2). Revenue per capex $ is held flat across generations because Ornn prices old and new chips at about the same $ per PFLOP-hr [26]. Steady-state capex ~46% of revenue.

inputs_detail.value: Deducted as a cash cost: 5% of revenue in 2027, 4.5% 2028, 4% 2029, 3.5% 2030, 3% after
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2-26 SBC $165M = 6.4% of revenue, excluded from adj. EBITDA (8-K Ex.99.1); 10-Q shows $1.7B unrecognised RSU expense over ~3 years. The fade follows the supervisor's path.

inputs_detail.value: 0% through 2029; 21% of (EBITDA - SBC - 6-yr straight-line tax depreciation) from 2030
inputs_detail.derivation: Unchanged from round 2.
Unchanged.

Round-2 bridge of $64B, less ~$2.5B to fix the supervisor-flagged mix of the accrual FY guide ($37B) with H1 cash PP&E ($14.1B). Q2 accrual capex was $9.4B vs $6.4B cash, so H1 accrual ran ~$2.5-3B above cash and that amount should not be counted again as H2 cash. Range $58-65B; each $5B is ~$8/share.
Unchanged (551.5M + 35M ATM + net options/RSUs).

inputs_detail.value: Cohorts 2023-27 = ~3.94 GW-equivalent ($40.6B contract-price capacity / $10.3M per MW): 2023-24 468 MW (legacy colos: Plano, Chester, Hillsboro, Douglasville, TierPoint, Las Vegas, Chicago, NJ/NY, Hammond existing, Crawley, Docklands, part of other US AZs); 2025 917 MW (Core Scientific Denton/Muskogee/Marble/Austin, Helios I, Polaris Forge B1, Norway, Sweden, Spain, Denmark, Cambridge ON); 2026 1,331 MW (Polaris B2, Dalton, Calgary, DataVita, Cheyenne, Helios II, Kenilworth ph.1, Lancaster, Bell SK, NJ JV); 2027 1,223 MW (Polaris third building, Helios III, Indonesia, Niagara, two development JVs). Unnamed residual ~500 MW sits in 'other US AZs'. Total with the two self-builds = ~4.3 GW vs 4.2 GW contracted power.
inputs_detail.derivation: MW and timing from the inventory [33]; undisclosed-MW sites given MW so that energised MW sum to the >1.85 GW year-end-2026 guide [1,2] and contracted to ~4.2 GW [3]. Allocations for undisclosed sites are judgment; they move value between rows, not the total.

inputs_detail.input: Revenue per MW at contract price
inputs_detail.value: $10.3M per MW-yr
inputs_detail.derivation: Exit-2026 run-rate guide $18.5-19.5B over >1.85 GW. The $40M/MW on Q3-26 short-dated deals [3] is not used for the fleet (company-defined on 3-6-month contracts, volume undisclosed).

inputs_detail.value: Generic fixed site cost 30%/28% of contract revenue embeds $1.8M/MW-yr rent + ~$0.6M power + ~$0.7M site ops. Core Scientific sites -3.5pp (rent $1.44M), Galaxy +1.0pp ($1.9M), Applied Digital 0 ($1.8M), Blockfusion +3.9pp ($2.2M, LOI). Owned self-builds: -14.6pp (no rent, +$0.3M property/maintenance) but +$6M/MW shell capex
inputs_detail.derivation: Rent per MW from landlord disclosures as compiled in the inventory (CORZ ~$850M/yr over 590 MW; Galaxy >$1B/yr over 526 MW; APLD ~$11B over 400 MW and ~15 yrs; Blockfusion $2.8B over 15 yrs on 85 MW). Kenilworth $322M purchase + ~$1.8B project for up to 250 MW = ~$8.5M/MW, less ~$2.5M/MW of fit-out that leased sites also pay inside k = ~$6M/MW (judgment).

inputs_detail.value: Kenilworth ph.2 (200 MW, 2028) 0.7; Hammond self-build (180 MW, 2029) 0.6; powered land/options/LOIs (1.5 GW, 2028-30, half owned) 0.5; NVIDIA framework increment above 5.7 GW to the 8 GW target (2.3 GW, 2029-31) 0.2. Each net of capex at k and shell capex, discounted at WACC.
inputs_detail.derivation: Kenilworth: owned, under construction, NJ EDA award up to $250M conditional on 10 years (credited at p0.6). Hammond: development agreement filed Jun-2025, no timing disclosed. Powered land/LOIs: the company itself counts them toward 8 GW [2], but they need ~$40B+ of capex while CoreWeave already funds $35-40B a year at ~9% unsecured, and a 750 MW Poolside commitment fell away in Apr-26 [33]. NVIDIA framework: 'subject to future agreements', no sites; only the increment not already in contracted power or powered land is counted, so no MW is counted twice.
Helios II slipped ~1 year to H1-27; Polaris third building and Lancaster ~mid-2027; Indonesia ~2028; DDTL 3.0 tests were moved 'to align with delivery schedule' [33]. Costs -$0.6/share.

inputs_detail.value: Contracted (signed RPO, by tier): IG 8.1%, Jane Street 9.1%, OpenAI/Anthropic 10.1%, other/unnamed 11.0%, Q3-26 commitments 11.2%; blended 9.4%. Uncontracted/post-contract/pipeline/terminal: WACC 11.5%
inputs_detail.derivation: IG: DDTL 4.0 prices at SOFR+225 (~5.9% fixed in Mar-26) [34]; today's fixed equivalent ~2.25% + ~4.8% 3-4-yr swap (3y UST 5.00%, SOFR 3.87%) [31,32] = ~7.0%. At its 1.2x DSCR ~83% of contract cash flow is debt-like; the ~17% residual carries first-loss completion and operating risk at Ke 13.75%: 0.83x7.0 + 0.17x13.75 = 8.1%. OpenAI-backed DDTL 3.0 at S+400 [35] -> ~8.8% fixed, 1.35x DSCR -> 0.74x8.8 + 0.26x13.75 = 10.1%. Jane Street (Fitch BBB-, Moody's Ba1, S&P BB; no secured facility disclosed): midpoint 9.1%. Other/unnamed: DDTL 5.0 S+450 [37] -> ~10.5%, rounded up for unknown credits to 11.0%. Q3-26 commitments (customers and term undisclosed): DDTL 5.5 S+550 [36] -> 11.2%. WACC 11.5% unchanged (Rf 5.29% [7], ERP 4.23% [16], beta 2.0, Kd 9%).

inputs_detail.value: Meta ~$33.7B (orders $14.2B + ~$21B less ~$1.5B recognised), NVIDIA ~$6.0B, Microsoft ~$7B, Jane Street $6.0B, OpenAI ~$18.9B ($22.4B less ~$3.5B recognised), Anthropic ~$5B, other ~$27.1B. Remaining after 10/1/27: 74% of each ($77B), recognised 2027Q4-2032 on the 10-Q timing (41% 0-24 m, 39% 25-48 m, 20% 49-78 m)
inputs_detail.derivation: Contract values from the 8-Ks [38,39,40,50] and PRs [41]; recognised-to-date amounts, Microsoft's remaining balance and Anthropic's size ($4-7B analyst range) are judgment. Each tier's net cash flow = its revenue x the model's contract-price margin after site costs, overhead, SBC and tax (~55%). Tiers are recognised pro rata; Meta's orders run to 2031-32, so a back-loaded Meta profile would add a little more.

inputs_detail.value: Two development JVs: $1.7B committed, $479M carried -> $1.22B unfunded; NJ campus JV: up to $160M ($57M contributed) plus a $95M guarantee
inputs_detail.derivation: Unfunded commitments are deducted in the JV rows and the JV stakes are credited at 75% of contributions (wrong-way risk: the JVs' tenant is CoreWeave). Net +$0.09 and -$0.02 per share, so net debt stays $61.5B; the VIE maximum loss of $1.8B is the downside if the JVs fail.
Unchanged from round 3. Pipeline weighting changes only post-Oct-27 capex, so the Oct-27 bridge is unaffected.

inputs_detail.value: Round-3 reported -$56 -> rebuilt engine -$53 -> site leases/ownership -$50.8 -> pipeline probability-weighted -$28.9 -> delivery delay -$29.5 (single-rate) -> split-rate -$27.3. Sum of the 45 site rows $83.8 + terminal capacity growth after 2032 -$12.7 - net debt $98.4 = -$27.3 (the JV-row adjustments add +$0.07)
inputs_detail.derivation: Each step re-runs the full model. The largest change is not the discount rate but the pipeline: round 3 had ~2.65 GW of new capacity by 2032 at certainty and k 2.5, which earns ~7% unlevered against 11.5% and so destroyed value.

inputs_detail.input: Floored grid (per share at 2027-10-01; life weights 5y 0.20 / 6y 0.45 / 7y 0.25 / 8y 0.10; k weights 2.3 0.25 / 2.5 0.50 / 2.7 0.25)
inputs_detail.derivation: Weights unchanged from round 3. Flooring each cell understates the option value of limited-liability equity (supervisor), so $9 is a low estimate of the cash-flow value.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 6.0x x $20.3B NTM adj. EBITDA at 2027-10-01 = $121.9B EV less $61.5B net debt = $60.4B / 625M = $96.6, shown as $97.

inputs_detail.derivation: From the site-built cohort model: 25% of 2027 ($15.3B) + 75% of 2028 ($22.0B). Down $0.1B from round 3 because the 2027 cohort now ramps later (Helios II, Polaris third building, Lancaster slippage). The pipeline weighting does not touch 2028 EBITDA. Adjusted EBITDA excludes SBC, matching how the multiple is quoted.

Unchanged. The GPU-life debate (Burry, Kerrisdale since 2025 [27]) is public and already in the ~6.3x the market pays today; current rental indices are firm [25,26], so the research gives no reason to move the multiple over the next 12 months. Round 4: unchanged; the site work changes long-dated cash flows, not the next-twelve-month multiple.
Unchanged. JV commitments (~$1.3B unfunded) are not added because the JV stakes are worth roughly what remains to be paid (see DCF).
Unchanged.

bear.story: Includes a 7% distress leg centred near $17 (raised from 4% per the supervisor: ~$61B Oct-27 net debt, CDS ~811bp, ~$20B+ 2027 external funding). Core bear (21%, ~$43): Blackwell/Rubin supply catches up with power, Hopper and early-Blackwell rents slide toward the glut path (5-yr life), and the first big renewals of 2025-26 cohorts in 2028-30 visibly reprice. Investors start to apply the cohort math, the multiple compresses to ~4.5-5x on ~$20B NTM EBITDA, and funding costs rise. Site evidence adds two concrete paths: delivery slips (Helios II already a year late; the 2027 cohort sits on Polaris B3, Lancaster, Bell SK and Indonesia, all first-of-kind or mid/late-2027) and landlord concentration (Core Scientific 590 MW, Galaxy 526 MW, Applied Digital 400 MW = ~36% of contracted power) with 12-15-yr rent that has to be paid whether or not GPUs are re-leased.

base.story: Execution on plan (2027 revenue ~$25-26B, exit-2027 run-rate ~$30B). Rental indices stay firm because supply is short through 2027, so the repricing in the cohort DCF has not started by the horizon. The stock trades on ~6x NTM adj. EBITDA, minus dilution and higher net debt; median ~$79, a bit below spot, above my blended fair value. Site check: ~3.9 GW of the 4.2 GW contracted power is covered by named or allocated sites already funded through the 2026-27 capex; 2028+ growth depends on the 1.5 GW of powered land and LOIs, which I weight at 50%.

bull.story: Scarcity persists: A100/H100 keep re-contracting near original prices (7-8-yr life path), Rubin ships at record pricing, credit improves and the multiple re-rates toward 8x; the stock revisits the $150s. Even here the DCF only reaches ~$15-50/share, so the bull case is a multiple and momentum story, not a DCF story. Site upside: the 1.5 GW of powered land/LOIs plus the NVIDIA framework fill on IG contracts financed DDTL-4.0 style; the DCF at a 7-8-yr life and split rate reaches ~$16-33/share at k 2.5.

thesis_break_reason: $48, moved from $45 to the supervisor's reconciled level: ~21% below the $60.55 July-2026 low, ~$30B of equity on ~$45-48B early-2027 net debt and ~$61.5B by Oct-27, ~4.5-5x NTM adj. EBITDA. A sustained close there would most likely mean a funding failure, a cut from Customer A (40% of H1 revenue), or the market starting to price the glut path: older-generation rents falling toward cash cost, which takes economic life to ~5 years, where my DCF is deeply negative. The GPU-life research makes the last cause more concrete, which is part of why I narrowed the gap to spot. Round 4: unchanged. A sustained close at $48 would now most likely also coincide with a site-level failure (a landlord such as Blockfusion or Galaxy missing delivery, or the 2027 cohort slipping into 2028).

key_uncertainties: GPU economic life in a non-scarce market: per-share split-rate DCF at k 2.5 is -$75 (5 yrs), -$27 (6), +$16 (7), +$33 (8).
Capex intensity k: k 2.3 vs 2.7 is ~$60/share at any life; k and life decide whether the equity has DCF value.

Pipeline conversion: each 0.1 of probability on the 1.5 GW powered land/LOIs is ~-$1/share at k 2.5 (negative because new cohorts earn ~7% vs 11.5%), but would be positive if those MW are contracted with IG counterparties and project-financed like DDTL 4.0.
Site delivery: 2027 cohort sites (Polaris B3, Lancaster, Bell SK, Helios III, Indonesia, Niagara) and landlord concentration (Core Scientific, Galaxy, Applied Digital ~36% of contracted power).
Funding path: net debt ~$61.5B at Oct-27 (range $58-65B), ~9% marginal cost; each $5B is ~$8/share.
Counterparty mix of the backlog: Customer A 40% of H1-26 revenue, Customer B 23% (unnamed); OpenAI (~$19B left) is unrated and its facility was amended for delivery delays.
reasoning: Round 4 (sites and split discounting). (1) Sites: I mapped every inventory row into the cohort DCF. The 2023-27 cohorts ($109.5B capex at k 2.7, ~3.94 GW at $10.3M contract revenue per MW) are the contracted fleet; each site gets MW (inventory figures; undisclosed MW allocated so energised MW meet the >1.85 GW YE26 guide and the total meets 4.2 GW), a cohort by energisation date, its own rent (Core Scientific $1.44M vs $1.8M generic per MW-yr, Galaxy $1.9M, Blockfusion $2.2M) and, for owned self-builds, shell capex instead of rent. Conflicts: Dalton 175 MW (CORZ slides; equals 590-437 billable plus phase 1), Austin 20 MW (landlord slides), Kenilworth 250 MW campus phased 50 MW contracted + 200 MW probability-weighted, Niagara 85 MW from the LOI. Exited Poolside Horizon and the Core Scientific merger carry zero. Mining/HPC overlap does not arise (CoreWeave mines nothing); the NVIDIA framework counts only the 2.3 GW above contracted power plus powered land. Uncontracted pipeline is probability-weighted at WACC (expected 1.46 GW by 2031 vs ~2.65 GW certain in round 3), which lifts the base cell from -$51 to -$29 because new capacity at k 2.5 earns ~7% unlevered, below the 11.5% WACC. JV commitments are deducted in their rows. (2) Discounting: signed RPO ($77B left after Oct-27) is discounted by counterparty tier, with IG at 8.1% (DDTL 4.0 S+225 re-based to today's ~4.8% swap, plus a 17% first-loss residual at Ke) and OpenAI/Anthropic at 10.1% (DDTL 3.0 S+400). The blend is 9.4%. That adds only $1.35B ($2/share) because the remaining contract cash is near-dated; the post-contract tail, refresh and pipeline stay at 11.5%. DCF: base -$29.5 single / -$27.3 split; floored grid $8.1 / $8.9 (round 3: $4). The 5-yr case now runs the 6-yr contract slice to term (supervisor). Fair value $53 (was $51) = 0.5x$9 + 0.5x$97. Ladder: unchanged. The DCF still says the equity has value only if prices hold for 7+ years, the 12-month price is set by the ~6x multiple, and nothing in the site inventory falls due before Oct-27 that I had not already priced (Helios II and the 2027 deliveries are inside the base case). Thesis break $48 and the 1-month ladder are unchanged. Research this round: one web search (Q3 date, none announced), direct reads of the DDTL 4.0 deck, the 9/17 release, H.15 Treasury yields and NY Fed SOFR; the GPU-life facts were re-checked against the fact-check file (Kerrisdale not verifiable, so it is not relied on).

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Contracted 90% at contract price for 4/5/6 years (45/27/18% of each cohort), 10% at market from day one. Market price relative to contract by year of service: base 1.00, 0.90, 0.82, 0.78, 0.75, 0.58, retire after year 6 (year-7 ~0.42 is about cash break-even of ~0.33). 5-yr: 1.00, 0.80, 0.65, 0.55, 0.45 (6-yr contract slice now held at contract price to term). 7-yr: 1.00, 0.97, 0.94, 0.92, 0.90, 0.75, 0.60. The steep part (-50% vs launch spot in the ~2 years after the successor ships) falls inside the contract term because contract prices start ~40-45% below launch spot; ~-10%/yr after.
gpu_life.note: Per-share equity at 2027-10-01, UNFLOORED, split-rate, k 2.7->2.5, SBC deducted, $61.5B net debt, site-built with probability-weighted pipeline. Single-rate: -78 / -29.5 / +14 (8-yr +31). Floored basis (each value max 0): 0 / 0 / 16 split, 0 / 0 / 14 single. Round 3 was -128 / -56 / -5 unfloored. Most of the change comes from probability-weighting the pipeline and fixing the 5-yr contract break; the split rate adds ~$2-3. Company book lives per the fact-check: CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5, IREN 5 years.

discounting.basis: Contracted rate applies only to signed backlog: $103.7B RPO at 6/30/26 ($77B left after 2027-10-01) plus the >$25B Q3-26 commitments. Tiers: IG (Meta Aa3/AA-, NVIDIA Aa1/AA, Microsoft Aaa; ~$46.7B) 8.1% = DDTL 4.0 SOFR+225 re-based to today's ~4.8% 3-4-yr swap (~7.0%) on the ~83% debt-like share at 1.2x DSCR, plus a 17% first-loss residual at Ke 13.75%; Jane Street (BBB-/Ba1/BB, $6B) 9.1%, midway; OpenAI/Anthropic (unrated, ~$23.9B) 10.1% from DDTL 3.0 S+400 at ~1.35x; other/unnamed (~$27.1B) 11.0% from DDTL 5.0 S+450; Q3-26 commitments (customers/term undisclosed) 11.2% from DDTL 5.5 S+550. 9.4% is the $-weighted blend. Cash flow per tier = recognised revenue x contract-price margin after site cost, overhead, SBC and tax (~55%). Post-contract tails, contracts not yet signed, refresh, pipeline and terminal at the 11.5% WACC. Values are per share at 2027-10-01 for the base cell (6-yr, k 2.5): single -29.5, split -27.3 (+$1.35B, of which IG $0.97B). The floored, weighted grid gives the method values $8.1 single / $8.9 split. Discounting every tier at its bare debt cost (IG 7.0%) would give -26.2. The uplift is small because by Oct-27 the signed contract cash flows are 0-5 years out.
